key_insight: Trials that required English proficiency enrolled fewer Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants, while explicit language accommodation was uncommon.
clinical_relevance: Reviewing and revising language eligibility criteria could be a practical way to improve trial inclusivity and better align enrollment with diversity goals.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of US interventional ClinicalTrials.gov trials with posted results.
Eligibility criteria were mined with validated regex classifiers for English-language requirements and language accommodation.
Enrollment composition was modeled with adjusted generalized linear models accounting for trial and site characteristics.
evidence_signal: Among 44,487 US-site trials, 12.9% had an English-language requirement; it was linked to lower enrolled proportions of Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants.
watch_item: This is observational registry-based evidence, so associations may reflect unmeasured trial or site factors rather than direct causal effects.
paper_title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
